    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    customers_list = list(instance["customer_ids"])
    customers = set(customers_list)
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    vehicle_hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", len(customers_list))

    def route_load(rt):
        s = 0
        for n in rt:
            s += demands[n]
        return s

    def route_cost(rt):
        if not rt:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][rt[0]] + matrix[rt[-1]][depot]
        for k in range(len(rt) - 1):
            c += matrix[rt[k]][rt[k + 1]]
        return c

    def total_cost(routes):
        return sum(route_cost(r) for r in routes)

    # Construct initial feasible solution: Clarke-Wright savings with capacity and end constraints.
    # If something goes wrong, fall back to incumbent greedy.
    try:
        # Map each customer to an initial route id
        routes = {i: [i] for i in customers_list}
        parent = {i: i for i in customers_list}  # representative for route membership

        def find_rep(node):
            return parent[node]

        def set_rep(oldrep, newrep):
            # update representative for all nodes currently in oldrep route
            # deterministically by scanning nodes (kept compact; OK for <= few hundred)
            for x in customers_list:
                if parent[x] == oldrep:
                    parent[x] = newrep

        # Precompute loads
        loads = {i: demands[i] for i in customers_list}

        # Compute savings
        # savings(i,j)=d(depot,i)+d(depot,j)-d(i,j)
        pairs = []
        cl = customers_list
        m = len(cl)
        for a in range(m):
            i = cl[a]
            di = matrix[depot][i]
            for b in range(a + 1, m):
                j = cl[b]
                s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
                pairs.append((s, i, j))
        pairs.sort(reverse=True)

        for s, i, j in pairs:
            ri = find_rep(i)
            rj = find_rep(j)
            if ri == rj:
                continue
            li = loads[ri]
            lj = loads[rj]
            if li + lj > capacity:
                continue
            route_i = routes[ri]
            route_j = routes[rj]

            # Check if i and j are compatible ends (standard CW)
            i_at_start = route_i[0] == i
            i_at_end = route_i[-1] == i
            j_at_start = route_j[0] == j
            j_at_end = route_j[-1] == j

            merged = None
            # Case: i at end of route_i and j at start of route_j => append
            if i_at_end and j_at_start:
                merged = route_i + route_j
            # Case: i at start of route_i and j at end of route_j => prepend
            elif i_at_start and j_at_end:
                merged = route_j + route_i
            # Case: i at start and j at start => reverse one then append
            elif i_at_start and j_at_start:
                merged = list(reversed(route_i)) + route_j
            # Case: i at end and j at end => append with reversed j
            elif i_at_end and j_at_end:
                merged = route_i + list(reversed(route_j))

            if merged is None:
                continue

            # Apply merge
            newrep = ri
            oldrep = rj
            routes[newrep] = merged
            loads[newrep] = li + lj
            del routes[oldrep]
            set_rep(oldrep, newrep)

        # Collect routes
        sol_routes = []
        reps_seen = set()
        for i in customers_list:
            r = find_rep(i)
            if r in reps_seen:
                continue
            reps_seen.add(r)
            rt = routes.get(r, [])
            if rt:
                sol_routes.append(rt)

        # If merges left us with empty routes (shouldn't), rebuild by incumbent greedy for remaining.
        if not sol_routes:

        # If too many routes, try deterministic relocation to reduce count (still feasible-only).

        used = set()
        for rt in sol_routes:

            routes.append(route)

        if len(sol_routes) <= max(1, int(vehicle_hint * 0.95)):

            pass

    # Deterministic: evaluate moves in a fixed order; apply the first improving move found; repeat limited times.
    def delta_relocate(from_rt, to_rt, pos_from, pos_to):
        # move x = from_rt[pos_from] into to_rt at position pos_to (pos_to in [0..len(to_rt)] insertion)
        x = from_rt[pos_from]

        # Cost change for from_rt when removing x
        n = len(from_rt)
        prev_from = from_rt[pos_from - 1] if pos_from - 1 >= 0 else depot
        next_from = from_rt[pos_from + 1] if pos_from + 1 < n else depot
        old_from = matrix[prev_from][x] + matrix[x][next_from]
        new_from = matrix[prev_from][next_from]

            old_to = 0 if m == 0 else matrix[prev_to][next_to]
            new_to = matrix[prev_to][x] + matrix[x][next_to]
        elif pos_to == m:
            prev_to = to_rt[m - 1] if m > 0 else depot
            next_to = depot
            old_to = 0 if m == 0 else matrix[prev_to][next_to]
            new_to = matrix[prev_to][x] + matrix[x][next_to]
        else:
            prev_to = to_rt[pos_to - 1]
            next_to = to_rt[pos_to]
            old_to = matrix[prev_to][next_to]
            new_to = matrix[prev_to][x] + matrix[x][next_to]

        # Total delta = (old_from - new_from) + (old_to - new_to) ; positive means improvement.
        return (old_from - new_from) + (old_to - new_to)

    # One small relocation loop with restart based on earlier failures: if many routes, allow more moves.
    max_moves = 60 if len(sol_routes) > max(2, int(vehicle_hint * 0.8)) else 30

        for i in range(len(sol_routes)):

                    m = len(to_rt)

    used = set()
